text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mass Rapid Transit fares may be revised under a proposal aimed at persuading commuters to travel to the city before the morning rush hour and to use stored-value tickets.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu refuses to step down over police recommendations he be charged in a corruption scandal.
- Lawyer who acted for would-be buyers in a bungled Singapore $12.8 million property sale was mostly to blame, Court of Appeal says.
- Parliament will sit on May 26 in the first session of the Ninth Parliament.
- Singapore's key non-oil domestic exports for March likely to fall four percent from last year as result of continued poor demand for electronics.
- Singapore Press Holdings boosts interim net profit by 9.2 percent to S$172.4 million despite slower growth in advertising revenue.
- Neptune Orient Lines, which announced takeover bid for American shipping company APL Ltd this week, will decide within six months which vessel-sharing alliance to join.
- China removes last obstacle to direct sailings across the Taiwan Strait by approving six Taiwanese shipping companies to ply from Kaohsiung to mainland ports of Xiamen and Fuzhou.
- Bobby Ong Congqin, Singapore property developer accused of insider trading by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission will challenge suit and seek dismissal of complaint.

- The golden years of rapid export growth may be over for some of Asia's more successful economies as their income levels approach those of advanced countries and costs rise accordingly, Asia Development Bank warns.
- All 60 stockbroking companies in Malaysia have enough funds to meet losses incurred in the two weeks when market value of stocks listed on Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange dropped sharply.
